scenarios.text: A solo SaaS founder opens their company's Instagram page on a Sunday night and realizes the last post was six weeks ago, the day before a major product launch.
A freelance consultant wraps up a client project and sits down to write a LinkedIn post about it, only to spend two hours staring at a blank document and giving up.
A small ecommerce brand owner schedules time on Friday afternoon to film a TikTok, but the shoot runs long and the footage sits unedited through the entire weekend.
A two-person marketing team at an AI startup finishes a sprint and realizes they have no content queued for the next three weeks across any of their social channels.
A local gym owner gets a comment on their Facebook page asking if they are still open because there have been no posts in over a month.
An agency owner pitches a new client on social media management, then realizes they cannot keep up with content production for their own agency's accounts while handling client work.
A SaaS founder scrolls through a competitor's TikTok and counts seventeen short videos posted in the last month while their own account has none.
A bootstrapped startup team finishes their Monday standup and realizes that 'post something on social this week' has appeared on the to-do list for the fourth week in a row without getting done.
An ecommerce brand manager opens Hootsuite to schedule the week's content and finds the queue completely empty with nothing drafted or ready to upload.
A solo app developer launches a new feature update and wants to post about it across LinkedIn, Instagram, and TikTok but does not know how to adapt the same message for each platform's format.
